summary: @servicetitan/lazy-module preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React Suspense wrapper (src/index.tsx) but ships a preinstall dropper. package.json declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`, and setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB obfuscator.io-style blob (numeric/string constant array, rotator function, mangled identifiers, `with` statements requiring a non-strict runtime) whose filename bears no relation to the declared Suspense functionality. Fetching a second language runtime at preinstall solely to execute a large obfuscated sibling script is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the payload evades Node-based scanners by running under a freshly downloaded Bun. The tarball's package.json points repository at github.com/servicetitan/uikit and homepage at docs.st.dev, indicating the scoped identity of a real vendor; the dropper and obfuscated payload are grafted onto an otherwise-plausible library, consistent with a namespace-hijack or malicious release into the @servicetitan scope. Installing this version causes attacker-controlled obfuscated code to execute on the installer's machine under a downloaded Bun runtime.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
